title: ML fundamentals
description: The breadth interview: learning paradigms, linear models, trees and ensembles, optimization, evaluation, unsupervised learning, regularization, data handling, deep learning and statistics. Quick questions, small calculations and short written answers.

sources.title: AIMLInterviews (Alireza Dirafzoon, MIT)
sources.note: The interview guide whose ML fundamentals syllabus sets this course's topics.

sources.title: AIMLInterviews: ML fundamentals syllabus
sources.note: The topic list. Questions and rubrics here were written for this course.

tracks.name: Learning paradigms
tracks.summary: What learning from data means, which kinds of problems it solves, and the workflow every project follows.

tracks.name: Linear models and losses
tracks.summary: Least squares, the logistic model, the margin, and which loss fits which task.

tracks.name: Trees, ensembles, and optimization
tracks.summary: How trees split, how ensembles combine them, and how gradient methods take a step.

tracks.name: Evaluation and model selection
tracks.summary: Turning a confusion matrix into the right metric, and choosing a model without touching the test set.

tracks.name: Unsupervised learning
tracks.summary: Clustering, topics and projections: structure found without labels.

tracks.name: Generalization and data
tracks.summary: Bias, variance and regularization, and the data problems a training loss does not show.

tracks.name: Deep learning
tracks.summary: Parameter counts, backpropagation, recurrent cells, dropout and attention.

tracks.name: Statistics and distances
tracks.summary: Bayes, likelihood, R², p-values, and which distance suits which data.
